es: Reconocer si wish e if only hablan de una situación actual (verbo en pasado) o de un arrepentimiento pasado (past perfect).

teaching.en: I wish I lived closer to the school.
teaching.es: Ojalá viviera más cerca de la escuela.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + pasado simple habla del presente: ahora vives lejos.
teaching.audioText: I wish I lived closer to the school.

teaching.en: If only we could afford a bigger house.
teaching.es: Ojalá pudiéramos permitirnos una casa más grande.
teaching.explanationEs: If only = wish, pero más emotivo; could expresa lo que hoy no es posible.
teaching.audioText: If only we could afford a bigger house.

teaching.en: I wish I had left earlier yesterday.
teaching.es: Ojalá me hubiera ido antes ayer.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + past perfect (had + participio) es un arrepentimiento del pasado.
teaching.audioText: I wish I had left earlier yesterday.

teaching.en: If only I had taken that chance!
teaching.es: ¡Ojalá hubiera aprovechado esa oportunidad!
teaching.explanationEs: If only + past perfect: arrepentimiento fuerte por algo que no hiciste.
teaching.audioText: If only I had taken that chance!

teaching.en: I wish I were taller.
teaching.es: Ojalá fuera más alto.
teaching.explanationEs: Con wish se usa were con todas las personas: I were, she were.
teaching.audioText: I wish I were taller.

teaching.en: My biggest regret is not calling my grandmother more often.
teaching.es: Mi mayor arrepentimiento es no haber llamado más a mi abuela.
teaching.explanationEs: Regret (sustantivo) nombra lo que lamentas; wish + had + participio lo expresa.
teaching.audioText: My biggest regret is not calling my grandmother more often.
